subject: EdgeScale cutover — control-plane liaison checklist & post-cutover sanity sweep
messages:
From: Jordan Fleet <jordan.fleet@edgescale.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>; Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@edgescale.com>
Date: 2027-08-15T16:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Cutover dry-run next week / control-plane liaison

Thanks for running through options earlier. We did a short internal dry-run and have two items we want to lock with Redwood before the live swap: (1) control-plane failover timing and expected TTLs for upstream LB entries, and (2) which KV-cache priming step your runtime will trigger during the first 10m of traffic.

Can we get a concise liaison checklist that the EdgeScale ops team can attach to our change window? We want a clear point-by-point callout for whoever owns the control-plane cutover coordination (e.g., confirm BGP withdraw, confirm API gateway route propagation, confirm K/V priming).

Also attaching a short network layout (provisional) — we'll send the final diagram tomorrow after the routing team signs off.

—Jordan
Ops Lead, EdgeScale
[attachment: networking_diagram_edgescale.vsdx]

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Fleet <jordan.fleet@edgescale.com>; Ops Team <ops@edgescale.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-16T09:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Cutover dry-run next week / control-plane liaison

Jordan — thanks, this is helpful. I've pulled together a concise control-plane liaison checklist and a condensed runbook excerpt focused on the points you raised. High level items included:

- Pre-cutover: verify prefix announcement set, BGP session flaps tolerances, and LB health-probe TTLs (expected 30s)
- Cutover moment: trigger API gateway route swap, confirm upstream DNS TTL flush (120s), withdraw old BGP path once traffic is observed on the new path
- KV priming: Redwood runtime will run a prefix-based K/V cache warmup for the first 600s using the warmup set attached (prefetch rate capped to 250 tps to avoid backend overload)
- Fallbacks: automatic model fallback to smaller quantized variant for 15m if token latency > 450ms; manual rollback steps enumerated

I've attached the runbook PDF excerpt and the warmup set references. Please review the timings — the LB probe TTL and DNS flush windows can be tuned if EdgeScale needs shorter propagation.

Next step: can EdgeScale confirm who will be the on-call control-plane liaison during the change window? If you confirm, we will include name and contact in the final change ticket.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Senior Partnerships Manager — Redwood Inference
[attachment: runbook_controlplane_v3.pdf]

From: Jordan Fleet <jordan.fleet@edgescale.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-16T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Cutover dry-run next week / control-plane liaison

Camila — this looks good. Ops will designate Tara Greene as the liaison (t. greene@edgescale.com, +1-415-555-0199) and will own the primary BGP withdraw step. Two quick clarifications before we finalize the ticket: 

1) For the KV priming: can you confirm the warmup set will only prefetch model prefixes used by active routes (we want to avoid prefetching unused corp prompts)?
2) After the first 10 minutes, will Redwood keep the warm cache population for 1h or evict aggressively?

We will attach the signed change request to the HubSpot deal after we get your answers.

On the attachments: the runbook looks fine aside from one minor naming inconsistency on step 7 (I flagged in-line).

—Jordan

Subject: Re: Cutover dry-run next week / control-plane liaison — post-deploy smoke sweep attached

Quick post-cutover note: EdgeScale ran the swap in the 20:00–20:12 UTC window and we executed the liaison checklist as planned. Summary of validation steps and results attached: postdeploy_smoke_results_20270817.csv (high-level columns: check, expected, observed, status). Highlights:

- BGP withdraw observed within expected 45s (status: PASS)
- API route propagation measured at ~95s median (status: PASS)
- KV warmup reached 80% of warmset within 420s (status: PASS)
- Two transient 502s during minute 3 of cutover (status: WARN) — traced to a misconfigured LB health probe timeout; corrected and no further errors after 00:07 UTC

Action items:
- Camila / Ops: we should update step 7 naming to avoid ambiguity (Jordan already flagged a naming mismatch)
- Infra: add a guard to drop prefetch rate to 125 tps if backend 5xx rate > 1% during warmup
- Follow-up meeting: 2027-08-18 15:00 UTC for a 30m action review (I'll send calendar invite)

Nice work from everyone — the fallback behaved correctly when we saw the brief spike in token latency (auto-fallback triggered and fallthrough to quantized variant lasted 2m). Full CSV attached.

-- Rishi Malhotra
Director, Reliability Engineering — Redwood Inference
